title: Perfect coefficient dual pairs and shifted Tate-line stability
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, integers $a,n\ge1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$. Put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and choose $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. Fix a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum], let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme in its domain, and use the actual coefficient categories, tensor and internal Hom of [sk-def-sf-operations](i). Write $\mathbf1=\Lambda_X$, $H(P,M)=R\mathcal Hom_X(P,M)$ and $P^\vee=H(P,\mathbf1)$. The integral unit and tensor are completed; the field categories are the specified rationalization and common finite-stage categories, respectively. All tensor constraints and symmetries below are those of these categories, including their cohomological signs.

Let $P\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ be perfect, meaning dualizable as in [sk-def-perfect], equivalently site-perfect in the stage-specific sense of [def-weil-site-perfect-complex]. Let $m,s\in\mathbf Z$ and put $L=\Lambda_X(m)[s]$ using [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Then $P^\vee$ and $P^\vee\otimes L$ are perfect. The opposite-line evaluation maps give isomorphisms
$$L\otimes\Lambda_X(-m)[-s]\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf1,\qquad \Lambda_X(-m)[-s]\otimes L\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf1,$$
and tensoring with these two shifted lines gives mutually inverse functors preserving the perfect objects.

For any dual pair $(P,Q,e,b)$ with $e:Q\otimes P\to\mathbf1$ and $b:\mathbf1\to P\otimes Q$ satisfying both triangle identities, the transpose of $e$ is an isomorphism $Q\xrightarrow{\sim}P^\vee$ identifying $e$ with coefficient evaluation. Write $b_P:\mathbf1\to P\otimes P^\vee$ for the induced coevaluation. The canonical coefficient biduality
$$j_P:P\longrightarrow H(P^\vee,\mathbf1)=P^{\vee\vee},$$
defined as the transpose of $e_P\circ\sigma_{P,P^\vee}$, is an isomorphism. Its inverse is the composite
$$P^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{b_P\otimes1}P\otimes P^\vee\otimes P^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{1\otimes(\mathrm{ev}_{P^\vee}\circ\sigma_{P^\vee,P^{\vee\vee}})}P\otimes\mathbf1\cong P.$$
These are assertions about the actual coefficient evaluation and dual-pair maps in each of the four stages, not only about an abstract isomorphism of objects.

proof.text: Work in the actual coefficient tensor category specified in the statement. Its internal Hom is right adjoint to tensor, by clause (i) of sk-def-sf-operations; symmetry changes a left-tensor adjunction into the right-tensor convention used here. Choose a dual pair $(P,Q,e,b)$, possible by perfectness. The exact-pairing tensor adjunction gives $(-\otimes P)\dashv(-\otimes Q)$. Compare this with $(-\otimes P)\dashv H(P,-)$. Counit-compatible uniqueness of right adjoints gives $N\otimes Q\xrightarrow{\sim}H(P,N)$, whose untranspose is contraction with $e$. At $N=\mathbf1$, its component (after the unitor) is exactly $a:Q\to H(P,\mathbf1)$, the transpose of $e$, and $e_P(a\otimes1_P)=e$. Thus the assertion concerns the specified evaluation, not an unspecified object isomorphism.

source.place: proof, last sentence: perfect coefficient dual and coefficient biduality; returned Steps 3–4, including inverse Tate line

proof.text: Transport $b$ by $1_P\otimes a$ to $b_P:\mathbf1\to P\otimes P^\vee$. In the first triangle substitute $e_P(a\otimes1)=e$; it becomes the given first triangle. In the second conjugate the given identity of $Q$ by $a$, giving the identity of $P^\vee$. Apply the symmetric-swap leaf to this exact pair: $P^\vee$ has dual $P$, with evaluation $e_P\sigma_{P,P^\vee}$ and coevaluation $\sigma_{P,P^\vee}b_P$. In particular $P^\vee$ is dualizable, hence perfect in the stated convention. This also follows on the actual coefficient site from prop-sf-dualizable, whose hypotheses are precisely the site-perfectness assumed for $P$; thus the dual lies in the required coefficient domain at each stage.

source.place: proof, last sentence: perfect coefficient dual and coefficient biduality; returned Steps 3–4, including inverse Tate line

proof.text: Apply the right-adjoint comparison of step 1 to the swapped pair $(P^\vee,P,e_P\sigma,\sigma b_P)$. Its unit-target component is the transpose of $e_P\sigma$, namely the stated $j_P:P\to H(P^\vee,\mathbf1)$, so $j_P$ is an isomorphism. This uses the actual closed adjunction of the coefficient category and proves invertibility of this map, without identifying an arbitrary bidual isomorphism with it.

source.place: proof, last sentence: perfect coefficient dual and coefficient biduality; returned Steps 3–4, including inverse Tate line

proof.text:
Put $D=P^{\vee\vee}$, $A=P^\vee$, and $e'=\mathrm{ev}_A\sigma_{A,D}:A\otimes D\to\mathbf1$. Define $r=(1_P\otimes e')(b_P\otimes1_D)$, with unitors and associators. Naturality of symmetry and the transpose equation $\mathrm{ev}_A(j_P\otimes1_A)=e_P\sigma_{P,A}$ give $e'(1_A\otimes j_P)=e_P$, since $\sigma_{P,A}\sigma_{A,P}=1$. Hence
$$rj_P=(1_P\otimes e_P)(b_P\otimes1_P)=1_P.$$
Since $j_P$ is already invertible, $r=j_P^{-1}$, and therefore also $j_Pr=1_D$. This is exactly the inverse displayed in the statement; no independent choice of evaluation or coevaluation is involved.

source.place: proof, last sentence: perfect coefficient dual and coefficient biduality; returned Steps 3–4, including inverse Tate line

proof.text: The Tate line theorem gives local unit bases and opposite signed powers at all four stages; the twist-preservation theorem gives the finite-Tor domains and the opposite inverse twists. For the specified evaluations use more precise inputs: at finite coefficients the unbounded line-tensor theorem computes derived tensor by ordinary tensor with a flat line and identifies evaluation on a basis as $(au)\otimes(bu^*)\mapsto ab$. At integral coefficients apply the signed-line reduction/restriction theorem to $\mathcal O_E(1)$: the local freeness and the finite locally constant reductions required there are provided by the Tate line theorem. It identifies the ordinary line evaluation with the evaluation for the actual quotient-tower completed tensor. Thus for every integer $m$, including negative $m$, the two degree-zero opposite-line evaluations are isomorphisms of the actual coefficient objects. Their inverses provide the corresponding coevaluations.

source.place: proof, last sentence: perfect coefficient dual and coefficient biduality; returned Steps 3–4, including inverse Tate line

proof.text: Insert the opposite shifts. The signed total-tensor comparison $t_{s,-s}$ identifies $\Lambda(m)[s]\otimes\Lambda(-m)[-s]$ with $(\Lambda(m)\otimes\Lambda(-m))[0]$; use $t_{-s,s}$ in the other order. Composing these isomorphisms with the evaluations of step 5 gives precisely the opposite shifted-line evaluations. On the shifted degree-zero line factors the multipliers of both $t$ maps are $(-1)^{s^2}=(-1)^s$, because the first-factor degrees are $-s$ and $s$, respectively. The inverse evaluation and the other evaluation therefore contribute cancelling scalars in either triangle. The degree-zero line triangle then proves the shifted one. At integral coefficients the completed tensor-shift theorem identifies these comparisons with the finite-level signed maps on the strict quotient tower (and its product-cone shift), so the same cancellation takes place in the specified completed category, rather than in an uncompleted substitute.

source.place: proof, last sentence: perfect coefficient dual and coefficient biduality; returned Steps 3–4, including inverse Tate line

proof.text: For the field stages send the integral line, inverse line, evaluations and coevaluations through the prescribed raw rationalization, and then to a common finite coefficient field for $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. The completed scalar-line coherence theorem identifies the scalar-extended signed-line evaluations with the prescribed ones; its evaluation equation ensures they agree at every further common field. Composition preserves the two inverse and triangle equations. More explicitly a rational arrow is a finite sum $\sum f_i\otimes a_i$; each naturality square is the corresponding sum of the integral squares, by bilinearity. At the common stage any square is represented at one common finite field, and the scalar coherence equation makes the resulting equality independent of its enlargement. Thus the preceding inverse maps and natural tensor equivalences are maps of the actual rational and common-stage categories. This passage is used only for the line maps; the arbitrary dual pair and its coefficient transpose were treated intrinsically in steps 1-4.

source.place: proof, last sentence: perfect coefficient dual and coefficient biduality; returned Steps 3–4, including inverse Tate line

proof.text: Write $L^-=\Lambda_X(-m)[-s]$. For each $K$, reassociate $(K\otimes L)\otimes L^-$ and contract $L\otimes L^-$; the opposite contraction gives $(K\otimes L^-)\otimes L\cong K$. These maps are natural since tensor is a bifunctor; the line triangles proved above make the two tensor functors mutually inverse. Each line is site-perfect: locally it is a single shifted copy of the coefficient unit; its finite-Tor and constructible membership, and preservation of those domains, follow from twist preservation and the definition of finite Tor amplitude (a shift translates the bounding intervals). It is consequently dualizable. The tensor-pair leaf applied to any perfect object and $L$ or $L^-$ supplies an exact dual pair for its tensor, so both functors preserve perfect objects. Applying it to the perfect $P^\vee$ proves the remaining assertion $P^\vee\otimes L$ perfect.
